pageCache.pageTitle: Grange Park School - Our Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Values
At Grange Park School, we aim to work in partnership with our local community and are committed to providing a high-quality education in a safe, supportive and stimulating environment. We want to be a centre of excellence in all areas of school life. We value each pupil and aspire for them to be 'leaders of tomorrow.' Our royal blue uniform features our logo of an oak tree and the roots that are the foundation for them to flourish.
Our school motto is:
Strive - Lead - Succeed
Our Core School Values are:
We explore the values in depth and look at each one in turn for each month, focusing on people, stories, music and news that reflect the value.
The values, our school motto and logo are embedded through our behaviour for learning strategies; they are regularly discussed by staff and promoted through school assemblies and PSHE (Personal, Social and Health Education) lessons. We want our school community to ‘live’ our values.
The curriculum at Grange Park School also actively promotes fundamental British values. This includes the values of democracy, the rule of the law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance for others.
Our Vision and Values»

pageCache.pageTitle: Grange Park School - Welcome from the Headteacher
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Strive. Lead. Succeed.
It is my pleasure to welcome you to Grange Park School, a school where we are ambitious for every child and proud of everything our pupils achieve.
From the moment children begin their journey with us to the day they leave for secondary school, our aim is simple: to give them the knowledge, confidence, character and opportunities they need to succeed.
We believe children achieve their best when they are happy, feel safe and know that the adults around them believe in them. That is why we combine high expectations and excellent teaching with a caring, inclusive environment where every child is known, supported and challenged.
Our academic outcomes demonstrate those high expectations. In 2026, 97% of our Year 1 pupils passed the Phonics Screening Check, our pupils achieved an exceptional 24.59 out of 25 average in the Multiplication Tables Check, with 85% achieving full marks, and 83% of our Year 6 pupils achieved the expected standard in Reading, Writing and Mathematics combined.
But a Grange Park education is about much more than results.
We want our children to discover their talents and develop the confidence to try something new. Through sport, music, trips, clubs, leadership opportunities, swimming in our heated pool and our free 11+ preparation from Year 3, we work hard to provide experiences that broaden horizons and raise aspirations.
Our values are visible in the way our children learn, behave and treat one another. We want pupils to be kind and respectful, resilient when things are difficult and ambitious about what they can achieve.
Most importantly, we want children to enjoy their primary years. When they eventually leave Grange Park, we want them to take with them wonderful memories, strong friendships, a love of learning and the belief that their future is full of possibility.
There is no better way to understand our school than to experience it for yourself. I warmly invite you to visit Grange Park, meet our children and staff and see what makes our school such a special place to learn and grow.
Mrs Madar Headteacher
Strive. Lead. Succeed.

Pupils with SEND
The Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Co-ordinator (SENDCo) is Miss Allen.
At Grange Park Junior School, all pupils receive quality first teaching that is differentiated and personalised which enables them to make the best possible progress and feel that they are a valued member of the wider school community. We expect that all pupils with a special educational need and/or disability (SEND) will meet or exceed the high expectations we set for them through an enriched curriculum with a range of resources and strategies catered to our children.
As a school, we ensure that pupils with an additional need receive support, whilst having access to a broad and balanced curriculum. By working in partnership with families, it is our aim that pupils will become confident individuals that are able to make a successful transition on to the next phase of their education.
In the Classroom
Our pupils with a special educational need and/or disability (SEND) are supported through a range of scaffolds in the classroom. Our inquisitive learners have access to a variety of resources that enable them to meet age-related expectations through independent work and support provided by our staff. Our Help Desks in the classroom enable our children to confidently seek out resources that may benefit them in their learning.
At Grange Park Junior School, all pupils remain in the classroom for quality first teaching. We acknowledge that all pupils benefit from extra support which may come in the form of 1:1 support in the classroom, specific interventions and individual sessions. This enables us to respond to the needs of our learners whilst providing stability and structure to our pupils.
Our children are able to access speech and language therapy which is directed by the speech and language therapist and involves pupils working in groups to complete activities to support their speech and language needs. Through Occupational Therapy targets, our staff are able to continue with implementing support in the classroom. Our phonics interventions allow us to assess and support our learners who may require extra support in meeting the phonics requirements in KS1. In conjunction with interventions across the curriculum, where needed, our children are able to practise applying their skills.
Home and School Connections
In addition to this, all pupils on our SEND register will have an individualised Learning Plan. This is a document created together with the school, parents and child that gives pupils SMART targets to work on for a term. Our plans outline how our children will be supported to meet their targets at school, how families can support our learners at home and the expected outcomes. This is reviewed each term (in line with parents' evenings) with the school, parents and child, and a copy is sent home to promote home and school connections.
Should you have any further questions about Special Educational Needs and Disabilities at Grange Park Junior School, please feel free to contact Miss Allen on 0208 353 4265
sencogpjs@grangeparkjuniorschool.co.uk

Parent Pay
At Grange Park School, we provide a more convenient way to select school dinners and pay for clubs, items and trips by using a secure service called Parent Pay.
We no longer accept cash in school, however should this be an issue for you, please contact the school office.
Making secure payments online using your credit or debit card
Parent Pay offers you the freedom to make payments whenever and wherever you like, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week - safe in the knowledge that the technology used is of the highest internet security available.
You will have a secure online account, activated using a unique username and password; you will be prompted to change these, and to keep them safe and secure.
If you have more than one child at our school or children at other Parent Pay schools, you can create a single account login for all your children. A letter with activation details will be provided when your child begins school full-time.
Making a payment is straightforward and Parent Pay holds a payment history for you to view at a later date; no card details are stored in any part of the system. Once you have activated your account, you can make online payments starting straight away.
Parent Pay FAQs
When can I log in to my account?
Once you have received your activation letter from school with your activation login details you will be able to activate your account immediately and start making payments straight away.
Which cards can I use?
Parent Pay accepts MasterCard, Visa credit cards, and Maestro, Switch, Delta, Electron, Solo and Visa debit cards.
Is it safe to make payments on the internet?
Yes. Parent Pay uses leading technology to process your card transactions securely. All communication with the bank is encrypted and neither Parent Pay nor the school have access to your card details.
How can I check that it’s secure?
Standard website addresses begin with http: the address for a secure site will always begin with https. You will also see a padlock at the bottom/top right of the screen on our login page and after you have logged into your account; never enter your card details or personal data on any web page whose address does not start https.
What about our personal information?
Parent Pay holds a very limited amount of information about you and your child solely for the purpose of administering your account however; Parent Pay does not use your personal information other than for supporting the school. We do not share or give information to any other organisations. We operate under strict guidelines set out by the Data Protection Act 1998.
Protection against fraud
Parent Pay will NEVER contact you by phone, email or mail and ask you to divulge confidential information like passwords or card numbers. If you are ever contacted by someone claiming to be from Parent Pay, Please contact Parent Pay immediately on 02476 994 820.
Please visit www.parentpay.co.uk if you require any further information.

Pupil Premium
What is Pupil Premium funding?
At Grange Park School, we endeavour to support Pupil Premium children of all abilities across all areas of the curriculum.
Pupil Premium is additional funding for schools to raise the attainment of disadvantaged pupils of all abilities and to close the gap between them and their peers.
Service Pupil Premium (SPP)
There is also additional funding for supporting children and young people with parents in the regular armed forces. This is an allocation to offer mainly pastoral support during challenging times and to help mitigate the negative impact on service children of family mobility or parental deployment. Pupils attract the premium if they meet the following criteria:
one of their parents is serving in the regular armed forces
they have been registered as a ‘service child’ in the school census at any point since 2011
one of their parents died while serving in the armed forces and the pupil receives a pension under the Armed Forces Compensation Scheme (AFCS) or the War Pensions Scheme (WPS)
Schools will receive funding for each eligible pupil.
Further information about PP funding can be found by clicking the link below:

Wrap Around Care
Wrap Around Care phone number (3:20-5:45pm): 07 745 506 612 Wrap Around Care email address: wraparoundcare@grangeparkschool.co.uk
Click to view Grange Park Schools Wrap Around Care Parent Welcome Pack.
At Grange Park School, our Wrap Around Care provision aims to provide a safe, inclusive and nurturing environment where children feel happy, secure and valued at the end of the school day.
Our vision is to support children to strive for self-belief, lead through positive relationships and succeed by developing independence, resilience and empathy. Through high-quality care delivered by trusted school staff, we support children’s well-being while providing families with reliable, accessible and affordable childcare.
Wrap Around Care will run from 3:20pm until 5:45pm, Monday to Friday. We offer the following flexible session options:
Wrap Around Care is term time only.
How do I register & book?
All children must be registered before attending Wrap Around Care. To register your child, please fill out the following form, ensuring at least three emergency contacts are listed. Wrap Around Care Registration Form Once a child is registered for Wrap Around Care, bookings can be made. Bookings must be made at least 24 hours before the required care date (3pm the day before). If you have registered your child, please pre-book your sessions via ParentPay.
Bookings are only guaranteed once payment has been made via ParentPay.
Bookings made within 24 hours of the start time must be made by phone via the school office (020 8353 4265). Online booking is not available for late bookings. A £2 late booking fee applies, subject to availability. Late booking fees and session fees will also apply to any child who is placed into Wrap Around Care due to late collection after 3:30pm.
If an extension of a currently booked session is required with less than 24 hours notice, you must contact the Wrap Around Care team via mobile (07 745 506 612). The additional session charge will apply.
Cancellations must be made 24 hours in advance or charges may still apply. Please email wraparoundcare@grangeparkschool.co.uk at least 24 hours before to cancel a pre-booked space. Cancellations with less than 24 hours notice must be made via telephone to the school office (020 8353 4265) and will not be eligible for a refund.
If your child is absent from school, please notify the school office by phone (020 8353 4265). Charges will still be applicable for on-the-day cancellations. No refunds are given for missed sessions or early collection.
Collection arrangement at the end of the school day:
Parent Collection information:
If someone other than a parent/carer is collecting your child:
Late Collection Policy
Parents are encouraged to inform staff promptly via the Wrap Around Care phone number (07 745 506 612) if there is any delay in collection or a change in the person collecting their child. If a child is not collected by the end of their booked session, parents/carers will be charged the fee of the next bookable session. If a child is collected after close time (6pm), late collection charges will apply, per child. To ensure the safety and wellbeing of all children, the following late collection charges apply:
Grange Park School reserves the right to withdraw a child’s place following repeated late collections beyond closing time or non-payment of late pick-up charges. Parents/carers will always be informed in advance before a place is withdrawn for this reason.
Grange Park School believes it is important that children eat nutritious, tasty food as part of their overall development. Wrap Around Care meets all requirements of the School Food Standards 2016, including the provision of healthy, age-appropriate snacks.
The following food options will be available during Wrap Around Care:
Staff must be informed of any allergies or dietary requirements during registration. We are a nut-free school.
We offer a wide range of exciting, hands-on activities that give children fresh experiences and help to build self-belief, positive relationships, independence, resilience and empathy. Activities are planned around a range of themes, which may include topics such as World Athletics Championships, Animal Science or Feelings and Wellbeing.
New sessions are planned each week and link to different areas of the curriculum, ensuring children always have something new to explore. Activities may include arts and crafts, creative challenges or team games inspired by the weekly theme.
Each session follows a similar routine:
Children attending Wrap Around Care are expected to follow the school’s Behaviour Policy. Wrap Around Care behaviour expectations will be established with the children attending. They will be displayed and referred to regularly, particularly during Daily Welcome Meeting time. Persistent inappropriate behaviour may result in a review or withdrawal of a child’s place.
The provision aims to be welcoming, inclusive and open to all children. Staff are committed to making sure every child feels safe, valued and able to take part, whatever their individual needs or circumstances. Through careful planning, well-trained staff and close partnership with families, children are supported to feel confident, happy and successful in a caring and inclusive environment.
The provision is committed to ensuring that all children are cared for in a safe, happy and secure environment. Parents and carers can be confident that robust safeguarding arrangements are in place and that children’s well-being is always our highest priority. Grange Park School’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Policies and arrangements fully apply and can be found on the school website.
As a school-run provision, Wrap Around Care follows Grange Park School’s existing health and safety policies and procedures, ensuring consistency across the school day and beyond.
Parents/carers will be informed of any accidents or injuries upon collection. In the event of serious illness or injury, parents/carers will be contacted immediately and emergency services called if required.
As a school-run provision, Wrap Around Care follows Grange Park School’s existing policies and procedures along with Wrap Around Care guidance, ensuring consistency across the school day and beyond. These can be found on the school website and can be made available upon request.
To support affordability, the school has taken steps to ensure parents can access government childcare support schemes, such as Universal Credit Childcare, where eligible. Families should visit Best Start in Life - Best Start in Life or Check what help you could get with childcare costs - GOV.UK for more information.
